 Live .  7,359 viewing 7359 viewing Live page Updated 2 minutes ago US Grand Prix: Antonelli wins and needs two more points to seal title - reaction
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Leaderboard 
 Summary
 Kimi Antonelli wins US Grand Prix to be on brink of title
 Antonelli will secure championship in Mexico next weekend by finishing ninth or better
 George Russell eighth and Lewis Hamilton fourth in Austin
 Charles Leclerc second and Max Verstappen third
 Select 'listen live' for BBC Radio 5 Live commentary (UK only)
 Close form Send us your F1 views
 Get involved Live Reporting

 Well at least Kimi will be old enough to have a drink or two to celebrate in Mexico
 Nick, Newcastle upon tyne 
 10 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Verstappen - 'Our overall pace was not good enough' published at 22:24 GMT 22:24 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Red Bull's Max Verstappen speaking after finishing third: "I think our overall pace was not good enough and then probably also the tyres that we had available were probably not the right ones. It's something that we have to understand because I think the last few races it was always working well for us. For whatever reason it didn't work out here. We still managed to get on the podium, maybe a little bit lucky with the VSC at the end but I'll take it.
 On his overtake on Lando Norris: "I had to. It was either get overtaken or you have to go for the overtake so that's what I did."
 14 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 "Unfortunately, we came short on the victory' - Leclerc published at 22:20 GMT 22:20 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who finishes second in Austin: "It was quite a good race. Unfortunately, we came short on the victory, which is eventually our target, but at the end of the day, it was a positive race; we had a good pace. 
 "The first stint was a bit more difficult. Kimi [Antonelli] went for a one-stop which was not really on our cards to be honest. But we were in the race with Max [Verstappen] and we had good pace. 
 "It was a fun race with quite nice battles at the start and then later on with Lando [Norris] and Max. It was quite tricky but I enjoyed it. I really enjoyed it and I ended up with a little less battery and it was a bit difficult to protect to Max but I knew we had pace to keep fighting later on, which we did, so it's a good race overall."
 18 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:15 GMT 22:15 GMT 
 Damon Hill 
1996 world champion on BBC Radio 5 Live in Austin 
 Kimi Antonelli has an infectious personality. The team love him, he's enjoying everything he's got in F1 and he's very grateful for all the breaks they've given him at Mercedes. But he delivers. He's such a nice kid. It's incredible. 20 years old and he's on the verge of winning his first championship which I'm sure will be the first of many. 
 68 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Perfect execution' from 'the whole team' - Antonelli published at 22:12 GMT 22:12 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli speaking after winning the United States Grand Prix: "It was the result we needed to be fair and the whole team deserved it so much. All this time, putting in so much work on bringing this new package and finally seeing the results is very pleasant. Also perfect execution from the strategy team to call the one stop. Really happy that we made it stick and today was a team effort."
 On being just two points away from winning the world championship: "We're very close but we'll try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it soon."

 Team radio - Antonelli to Mercedes published at 22:04 GMT 22:04 GMT 
 Antonelli: "Good job everyone. That's the result we needed and let's keep pushing."
 90 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Champagne moment published at 22:02 GMT 22:02 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Well, not quite a champagne moment for Kimi Antonelli, as he's too young to drink in the United States. The 20-year-old is delighted, though, as the Italian national anthem rings out. 
 US Senator Ted Cruz doesn't get the warmest of welcomes from the Texas crowd as he hands Antonelli that fantastic winner's trophy. 
 The fans are also loving seeing Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen in the top three. Ferrari's Leclerc was second in Singapore, while Red Bull's Verstappen is on a run six podium finishes.

 Post published at 21:57 GMT 21:57 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Austin is Kimi Antonelli's ninth win of the season and now he needs only two more points to enter the history books as the youngest ever Formula 1 world champion. 
 "So, probably Mexico then?!" says Charles Leclerc to the Mercedes driver as the top three watch the highlights of today's race in the cooldown room. Antonelli just nods his head in reply. 
 Max Verstappen then responds with what we're all probably thinking: "Tequila!!"
 122 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'What a drive, what a win' - Lord published at 21:55 GMT 21:55 GMT 
 Mercedes' deputy team principal Bradley Lord speaking to 5 Live's Rosanna Tennant: "It felt like everyone was getting a bit excited but all Kimi could do today is go out and win. Amazing job by everyone on the pit wall and the strategists back at base because I think the one stop was about eight seconds quicker on our numbers but Kimi also finished plenty more than eight seconds ahead. What a drive, what a win." 
 On George Russell's weekend: "Difficult afternoon for him, very understeery car in that first stint. Came in and then couldn't make the pass on Piastri. George will be determined to put some highlight performances in for the rest of the season and help bring home the constructors' championship."

 Antonelli wins in Austin published at 21:46 GMT 21:46 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Lando Norris ends his time at Cota in fifth place after being overtaken by a few cars in the latter stages of the race. The other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar is sixth, Oscar Piastri is seventh and George Russell lives to fight another day in the title battle by finishing eighth. 
 Liam Lawson continues his points run in ninth and the Alpine of Pierre Gasly ends the grand prix where he started in 10th spot. 
 Pete Bonnington jokes with Kimi Antonelli he only got struck once for track limits. This lad's learning.

 Chequered flag published at 21:40 GMT 21:40 GMT 
 Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli wins the United States Grand Prix from pole position! 
 "Beautiful drive," says Antonelli's race engineer Pete Bonnington. 
 Charles Leclerc comes home in second place and Max Verstappen takes the final podium spot in third. The other Scuderia of Lewis Hamilton just ran out of time to make a move on the Dutchman and finishes fourth. 
 Image source, Getty Images 
 1162 138 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Final lap published at 21:39 GMT 21:39 GMT 
 Lap 56/56 
 The United States Grand Prix is almost at an end, and now the crowds in Texas are cheering Kimi Antonelli with every corner. 
 The Italian is only 20 years old, but he's on the brink of potentially becoming the new world champion when we head to Mexico next weekend.
